findings.quote: the consensus path and the free cash flow guide are consistent with each other and with the Q2 run-rate
findings.issue: Unsupported, and the page contradicts it for cash flow. The earnings release reports $6.4 million of free cash flow in Q2'26 alone, while the full-year guide is $12.0 million - $14.0 million. A Q2 run-rate is not consistent with that guide; it implies a much weaker second half or a lumpy quarter. The 50% Base weight rests on this sentence.
findings.fix: Drop the run-rate claim, or say plainly that Q2's $6.4 million is large against the full-year guide and explain what that means (a weaker second half, or conservative guidance). Argue the 50% Base weight on something the page supports.
findings.note: Run-rate claim is gone. Cash flow says Q2 is large against the guide, and the 50% Base weight is now argued from the guide being issued with half the year reported.

findings.quote: a company that has cut its way to cash generation
findings.issue: Causal claim the pack does not establish. The FCF Margin row shows the company was already cash-generative before any cuts (19.1% in FY22, 17.1% in FY24). The quarter's opex drop is almost entirely sales and marketing, which the report itself says is unexplained (see F-3).
findings.fix: Describe what the figures show without the causal story: for example, that free cash flow has been positive throughout the FY21-FY25 series while revenue has shrunk.
findings.note: Causal claim removed. On the corrected series analystCommentary now says free cash flow turned positive in FY24 after a negative FY23, which matches the FCF Margin row.

findings.quote: Our view is that the cost base has improved faster than revenue, which is a margin story, not a growth story.
findings.issue: Missing counter-case, and the conclusion goes against the paragraph's own caveat. The MD&A table on the page shows six-month sales and marketing of 8,438 (2026) against 17,888 (2025), against 4,677 and 14,346 for the quarter. So Q2'25 carried an unusually large sales and marketing charge, and Q1'26 to Q2'26 sales and marketing did not fall. The narrower operating loss (2,921 against 10,338) is mostly a weak comparison base, not cost improvement. The author says the decline is not a run-rate, then concludes the cost base 'has improved'.
findings.fix: Use the six-month figures to show that the year-over-year opex fall comes from an unusual prior-year quarter. Restate the view: the improvement in the quarter's loss is mostly a base effect, and the underlying cost base is roughly flat.
findings.note: Six-month figures used; the loss improvement is called a base effect and the cost base roughly flat.

findings.quote: the vendor shows no total debt for FY25
findings.issue: Over-reads a missing value. The Total Debt and Net Debt cells for FY25 are '—', meaning not reported, not zero. FY21 to FY24 show debt rounding to $0.0-0.1B. 'Shows no total debt' tells the reader the company has none, and the 'no solvency question' conclusion partly rests on that.
findings.fix: Say that the vendor table leaves FY25 total debt blank, so the report cannot confirm the debt position. Rest the liquidity view on the current ratios, which are on the page.
findings.note: Says the FY25 debt cells are blank and the debt position cannot be confirmed; the liquidity view rests on the current ratios.

findings.quote: The counter-case to a clean balance sheet is that the Q2 tender and open-market buybacks used cash that would otherwise have earned that interest.
findings.issue: Two problems. (1) It implies the buybacks explain the fall in other income (202 against 889), which the excerpt does not establish; the author admits the excerpt 'does not give the cause' one sentence earlier. (2) 'Open-market' is not on the surface. The release says only 'approximately 0.7 million additional shares repurchased at an average price of $1.63'. The Bear driver repeats it: 'the $1.63 average price the company paid for its open-market repurchases in Q2'.
findings.fix: Remove the causal link. Call the second tranche 'additional repurchases', not 'open-market', in both places. If a balance-sheet counter-case is wanted, use one that is on the surface, such as the fact that the quarter-end cash balance is not given.
findings.note: Causal link dropped; the balance-sheet counter-case is now the missing quarter-end cash figure; 'additional' used in the Bear driver.

findings.quote: excludes changes in settlement assets and liabilities from the Expensify Card program
findings.issue: Attaches a fact to a source that does not carry it. The release defines free cash flow as excluding 'changes in settlement assets, net and settlement liabilities'. It does not tie these to the Expensify Card program.
findings.fix: Quote the definition as written, without the Expensify Card attribution.
findings.note: Definition quoted as written.

findings.quote: Management guides fiscal 2026 free cash flow to $12.0 million - $14.0 million, below the FY25 level.
findings.issue: Source/definition disagreement chosen silently. FY25 free cash flow of $20.1M is the vendor's figure (operating cash flow less capex). The guide uses the company's own definition, which excludes settlement-asset changes, as the same paragraph notes. 'Below the FY25 level' compares two different measures without saying so, and the 'credible but declining' view depends on it.
findings.fix: State once that the $20.1M is the vendor's FY25 figure on a different definition from the company's guide. Either qualify the 'below FY25' comparison or drop it.
findings.note: Definitions distinguished; the report says it does not compare the guide with the vendor's figures.

findings.quote: the stock holds near the low end of the Street target range at $2.50
findings.issue: Calls coherence. (1) The Base is anchored to the low end of the sell-side range. That is not a multiple, a guided figure or an argued valuation, and the driver (revenue at consensus, FCF in guide) is never turned into a price. (2) 'Holds near' $2.50 is wrong: the stock is at $2.25, so Base implies about 11% upside, while the thesis says 'we see the price as roughly fair'. (3) No sentence explains the $2.00-$2.80 target band; nothing in the prose anchors $2.00 or $2.80.
findings.fix: Anchor the Base to something on the page, such as the FY27E or NTM P/E applied to consensus EPS, or an FCF-yield argument on the guide, and describe it as a move to the price rather than holding it. Add one sentence explaining how the $2.00-$2.80 band was set relative to the scenarios.
findings.note: Base is now 15x the midpoint of the FY26 free cash flow guide, turned into a price, and the thesis reads 'fair to slightly full'. The band brackets the Base. Problems with the new anchor are logged as F-27 and F-28; the unexplained low end of the band is logged as F-31.

findings.quote: Further share repurchases funded from operating cash flow (see Capital allocation).
findings.issue: Unsupported, and the section it points to contradicts it. Capital allocation says 'the release does not say whether further buybacks are planned'. Nothing on the surface says how the repurchases were or would be funded.
findings.fix: Replace it with a catalyst that Capital allocation argues, or reword it: 'Any new repurchase authorization, which the release does not yet announce'. Drop 'funded from operating cash flow'.
findings.note: Catalyst reworded to a not-yet-announced authorization; funding claim dropped.

findings.quote: A dual-class structure with a Voting Trust
findings.issue: Mischaracterizes the capital structure. The proxy shows three classes: Class A, LT10 and LT50.
findings.fix: Say 'a multi-class structure (Class A, LT10 and LT50)', or just 'LT10 and LT50 shares held in a Voting Trust'.
findings.note: Now 'multi-class structure'.

findings.quote: the stock has already moved from the bottom of its 52-week range to near the top
findings.issue: Unsupported. The 52-week range gives a low and a high, not the order they came in. The 30-day price history on the page shows the stock falling from about $2.64 on August 21 to $2.25. At $2.25 against $0.69-$2.81 the price is in the upper part of the range, not 'near the top'. The analystCommentary repeats 'near the top of the 52-week range'.
findings.fix: State the position without a path: 'at $2.25 the shares sit in the upper part of the $0.69 – $2.81 range'. Make the claim once (see F-14).
findings.note: Path claim removed; 'upper part of the range' used once, in analystCommentary.

findings.quote: The FY25 10-K risk factors list pricing pressure from competition and competitors' feature launches among the drivers of results. With gross margin down to 50.3% in FY25 from 62.4% in FY21, the margin history does not show pricing power.
findings.issue: Over-attribution and an unsupported inference. The risk factors list pricing pressure as something that 'may' cause results to fluctuate, not as a driver of reported results. The gross-margin slide is then read as a lack of pricing power. But the 10-Q MD&A attributes the margin decline to cashback contra revenue and software amortization, and the pack contains no pricing data.
findings.fix: Say the risk factors name pricing pressure as a possible source of fluctuation. Either drop the pricing-power inference, or note that the MD&A attributes the recent margin decline to cashback and amortization, so the series does not isolate pricing.
findings.note: Rewritten as a possible source of fluctuation; pricing-power inference withdrawn.

findings.quote: which holds 83.6% of voting power as of March 27, 2026
findings.issue: Stale fact whose age changes its meaning. All proxy ownership percentages are as of March 27, 2026, before the Q2 repurchase of about 6.8 million Class A shares (an approximately 7% reduction). That repurchase changes the denominators for the 83.6%, 36.7%, 48.9%, 11.2% and 7.3% figures. The dates are given, but the report never says the figures predate the buyback.
findings.fix: Add one sentence that these percentages predate the Q2 repurchase, which reduced Class A shares outstanding and shifts ownership and voting percentages.
findings.note: Governance states the proxy percentages predate the Q2 repurchase.

findings.field: analystCommentary; sections.financials.incomeCommentary; sections.growth.points[0]; sections.growth.points[1]; sections.businessMoat.segments[0].body; sections.businessMoat.durability
findings.quote: The CEO's shareholder letter argues that New Expensify is the growth engine, citing revenue from net new customers up over 250% year over year to over $10 million ARR; the 10-Q itself does not break that business out, so we treat the claim as management's framing rather than a reported figure.
findings.issue: Cross-section repetition. The New Expensify ARR claim and its caveat ('not reported in the 10-Q') are argued in full in analystCommentary, growth.points[0] and segments[0].body. The 'revenue fell 5%' story recurs in analystCommentary, incomeCommentary, growth.points[1] and durability ('which declined in Q2'26'). Gross margin 48% from 52% appears in both analystCommentary and incomeCommentary.
findings.fix: Keep the ARR argument and caveat in Growth only, and point to it elsewhere. Introduce the Q2 revenue decline once in the income statement section and refer back to it in words.
findings.note: ARR argued only in Growth; the revenue decline and gross margin are introduced once in Income statement, with pointers elsewhere.

findings.quote: In other words, card adoption adds interchange but also adds contra revenue, so the card program does less for net revenue than the interchange line alone suggests.
findings.issue: Paraphrase repetition. The card story (interchange up 12% or to $5.9M, offset by cashback contra revenue, so net contribution is smaller) is argued in incomeCommentary, moatFactors[1] ('the card's net contribution is smaller than gross interchange'), growth.points[2] ('net card contribution grows more slowly'), risks.idiosyncratic[1], and again in the exec-summary risk. The Visa incentive decline appears in both incomeCommentary and risks.idiosyncratic[1]. The Bancorp dependence appears in companyOverview, moatFactors[1] and risks.idiosyncratic[3].
findings.fix: Argue the card net-economics mechanism once, in the income statement section. Moat should say what it means for lock-in, Growth should point back, and Risks should state only the forward risk and what to watch.
findings.note: Card mechanism argued once in Income statement; other sections point back. The Visa item appears once; Bancorp appears in companyOverview and as the forward risk only.

findings.quote: an installed Classic base that the CEO himself describes as a fixed pool that will naturally drain
findings.issue: Paraphrase repetition. The CEO's 'pool that will naturally drain' appears in durability and risks.idiosyncratic[0]. 'Paid members fell 2%' appears in moatFactors[0] and risks.idiosyncratic[0]. The 'path depends on migrating Classic customers and scaling acquisition' appears in leadership and growth.points[4]. The month-to-month contract terms appear in moatFactors[0] and risks.idiosyncratic[2].
findings.fix: Make each claim once and refer back in words. For example, keep the drain quote in Durability and have the risk bullet point to it and say what to watch.
findings.note: The drain quote, the paid-members figure, the path statement and the contract terms each now appear once.

findings.quote: the cash flow supports the floor
findings.issue: Repetition of the FCF-as-floor claim and its figures. Q2 free cash flow of $6.4 million and the $12.0 million - $14.0 million guide appear in analystCommentary, cashflowCommentary and the Base driver. 'Supports the floor', 'anchors our floor' and 'would remove the floor' recur across analystCommentary, cashflowCommentary and finalRecommendation. The thesis's 'Free cash flow guidance gives the equity real support, and the Q2 buyback shrank the share count' is restated in finalRecommendation as 'The free cash flow guidance and the Q2 buyback support the shares'.
findings.fix: Argue the floor once, in Cash flow. Have the analyst commentary and final recommendation point to it without restating the figures or the wording.
findings.note: Q2 FCF and the guide are argued in Cash flow; the guide range reappears only as the Base driver's anchor, which is where an anchor belongs. analystCommentary and finalRecommendation point back without figures.

findings.quote: The Street's targets range from $2.50–$3.00, with a consensus of $2.83, and our Base case sits at the low end of that range.
findings.issue: Repetition within and across Valuation. The Street range and the Base/Bull anchors to it are stated in multiplesCommentary, both scenario drivers and scenarioCommentary ('anchored to the top of the Street range'). The consensus $2.83 is in analystCommentary and multiplesCommentary. The FY26E ~$135.9M 'another down year' is in thesis, growth.points[1] and the Base driver. The CEO's 'each product alone is worth more' valuation claim is in leadership, the Bull driver ('sum-of-the-parts framing') and scenarioCommentary.
findings.fix: State the scenario anchors once, in the drivers, and keep scenarioCommentary to the probabilities. Introduce consensus revenue once (Growth or Valuation) and the CEO's valuation claim once (Leadership).
findings.note: The Street figures, the consensus target, FY26E revenue and the CEO valuation claim each now appear once.

findings.quote: The proxy also discloses employment arrangements with Mr. Alvarez Divo, Mr. Mills and Mr. Vidal as related-party transactions, including $1,650,985.94 of cash compensation to Mr. Mills as Chief Product Officer from January 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026.
findings.issue: Restatement, not judgment. The related-party pay is listed but not read for the holder. It does not say why these employees are related parties (each holds LT10/LT50 shares and voting power per the proxy table: Mills 6.6%, Vidal 1.8%, Alvarez Divo 2.0%), or whether the amounts matter against the company's scale. The cent-level figure adds precision with no point.
findings.fix: Say what the arrangement means for outside holders, for example that the related-party employees are also Voting Trust participants, or drop the sentence. Use the figure only if it supports a view.
findings.note: Reads the related-party employees as LT holders inside the voting bloc; cent-level figure dropped.

findings.quote: Insiders' economic stake in Class A is modest relative to their voting control, which is the main governance tension for outside holders.
findings.issue: Paraphrase of governance's 'their protection rests on management's own economic alignment rather than on voting rights'. The same control-versus-economics point is made twice. Insider ownership also does not read Barrett's 36.7% for the holder (what that stake alone lets him do) beyond the group-level remark.
findings.fix: Make the control-versus-economics point once, in Insider ownership, and read Barrett's 36.7% and the group's 48.9% for what they allow. Keep Governance to board and trust mechanics.
findings.note: Control-versus-economics point made once, in insiderOwnership.

findings.quote: total operating expenses fell to 19,251 from 28,915 (in thousands)
findings.issue: Voice/units. The paragraph mixes '$33.9M', '$30.8 million' and raw thousands ('19,251 from 28,915 (in thousands)', '4,677 from 14,346', '7,211 (in thousands)', '202 from 889 (in thousands)'), which reads unevenly. Range formatting is also inconsistent ('$12.0 million - $14.0 million' against '$2.50–$3.00' and '$5.4 to $7.4 million').
findings.fix: Where the surface gives a figure only in thousands, introduce the unit once per paragraph ('in thousands of dollars, ...') and keep a single range style.
findings.note: Units introduced as 'In thousands of dollars'; dollar-million ranges use 'to', price ranges use a dash.

findings.quote: describing Q2 in glowing terms
findings.issue: Here the company's own phrasing is the point, and the report paraphrases it in loaded words.
findings.fix: Quote the letter: the CEO calls it 'the most exciting quarter in years'.
findings.note: Letter quoted directly.

findings.quote: the FY25 10-K risk factors (filed February 26, 2026)
findings.issue: Tic. The identical dating parenthetical appears in two consecutive risk entries.
findings.fix: Date the 10-K once in the Risks section and refer back to it as 'the same risk factors'.
findings.note: Dated once in idiosyncratic[3]; systemic says 'The same risk factors'.

findings.quote: Free cash flow has been positive in every year of the FY21–FY25 series, so cash generation is not new
findings.issue: Repetition introduced by the rewrite. The positive-FCF-every-year claim is stated in analystCommentary, then restated in cashflowCommentary ('The vendor's FCF margin has been positive in each year from FY21 to FY25, ranging from 1.9% to 19.1%'). Likewise, the flat-consensus point is made in growth.points[1] ('imply a lower year than FY25 followed by a flat one'), again in scenarioCommentary ('consensus revenue is roughly flat between FY26E and FY27E') and in the thesis ('the Street expects little change through FY27E').
findings.fix: Argue the FCF series once, in Cash flow, and have analystCommentary point to it in words. Introduce the consensus revenue path once, in Growth, and have scenarioCommentary refer back to it ('the flat consensus path in Growth').
findings.note: The FCF series is argued only in Cash flow, and analystCommentary points to it. The consensus path is stated in Growth; the thesis and Base driver point to it. scenarioCommentary uses it in words as an argument for a lower multiple, which is acceptable.

findings.quote: so compensation decisions are not checked by an independent majority of votes
findings.issue: Unsupported inference introduced by the rewrite. The proxy excerpt says nothing about how executive compensation is set or approved: no compensation committee, no say-on-pay vote, no description of who approves these employment arrangements. Stockholder votes do not ordinarily decide individual pay, so the claim does not follow even from the voting figures.
findings.fix: Drop the sentence, or limit it to what the surface supports: the related-party employees are also LT holders whose shares sit in the Voting Trust, so they are inside the bloc that controls the vote.
findings.note: Compensation claim removed; governance says only that the related-party employees hold LT shares in the Voting Trust and sit inside the controlling bloc.

findings.quote: Barrett's stake alone gives him over a third of the vote, and the group sits close to a majority, so outside Class A holders cannot change the board or block strategy.
findings.issue: Faulty reasoning in the rewritten read. A group at 48.9% does not by itself stop outside holders; the operative fact is the Voting Trust's 83.6% of voting power, which Governance gives. As written, the conclusion is drawn from the wrong figure, and the reader is not told what Barrett's 36.7% lets him do (for example, block matters that need a supermajority), which the surface cannot support either.
findings.fix: Tie the 'cannot change the board' conclusion to the Voting Trust's 83.6% (pointing back to Governance). Describe Barrett's and the group's stakes as shares of that bloc, without claiming powers the excerpt does not describe.
findings.note: The control conclusion is tied to the Voting Trust's control of the vote, pointing back to Governance; no unsupported powers are claimed.

findings.quote: at 15x the midpoint of that guide, a multiple we assume for cash flow that consensus shows flat to lower, on ~91.19M shares, the stock is worth $2.14
findings.issue: Source disagreement on the share count, chosen silently, and the label depends on it. Base and Bear divide a total-dollar FCF value by ~91.19M, which the Quote line says is derived from market cap. The filings on the page point higher. The proxy counts 88,637,254 Class A, 4,209,827 LT10 and 8,175,283 LT50 shares as of March 27, 2026, before the ~6.8 million Q2 repurchase. The 10-Q table gives a Q2'26 basic and diluted weighted average of 95,441,380. The prompt's input check also flags the vendor market cap 10% below the cross-check (205M vs 229M). A higher count lowers Base and Bear in proportion. On either filing-based figure, the weighted value moves well below the line the report says is close. scenarioCommentary already says one turn less on the multiple derives SELL, so a gap of this size changes the call.
findings.fix: Say once that the vendor's derived share count and the filing figures disagree. State which count you use and why: for example, the 10-Q weighted average, or the proxy classes less the Q2 repurchase, described in words. Re-derive Base and Bear on that count and let the rule set the label. Do not re-tune the multiple or the weights to keep the current label; if the call changes, the prose changes with it.
findings.note: Addressed. scenarioCommentary states the disagreement once: the vendor-derived ~91.19M against the proxy classes less the Q2 repurchase and the 10-Q weighted average. It uses 95,441,380 with a reason and names the bias both ways. Base $2.04 and Bear $1.51 re-derive correctly on that count; E is -7.9%, so SELL is the derived label and the prose follows it.

findings.quote: a multiple we assume for cash flow that consensus shows flat to lower
findings.issue: Attributes a forecast to a source that does not carry it. The consensus on the surface gives revenue and EPS only (FY26E $135.9M / $0.12, FY27E $136.1M / $0.10). It has no cash flow estimate, so consensus cannot show cash flow as flat to lower. This sentence is the stated basis for the 15x multiple that the report says decides the call.
findings.fix: Base the multiple on what consensus actually shows, for example 'for a business whose consensus revenue is lower in FY26E and flat in FY27E, with EPS lower in FY27E (see Growth)'. Or base it on the company's own guide. Do not attach a cash flow view to consensus.
findings.note: Addressed. The 15x basis now cites consensus revenue lower in FY26E and flat in FY27E, with EPS lower in FY27E, all of which is on the surface.

findings.quote: free cash flow comes in no better than the low end of the guide; at 12x, a lower multiple we assume because a miss would show the decline outrunning New Expensify, the stock is worth $1.58
findings.issue: The Bear does not follow its own story. It prices free cash flow at the low end of the guide, which meets the guide, yet it justifies the lower multiple by 'a miss'. Most of the Bear's fall from the Base therefore comes from a multiple cut that is argued on an outcome the scenario does not assume. finalRecommendation treats a miss against the guide as a SELL trigger, which suggests a miss lies outside the Bear as priced.
findings.fix: Make the Bear consistent. Either price an outcome below the guide (a miss, argued on the Classic decline) and keep the miss rationale for the multiple. Or keep the low end of the guide and argue 12x on something that outcome actually shows, for example that a low-end result with revenue still falling (see Growth) gives no reason to pay the Base multiple. Re-check the SELL trigger in finalRecommendation against whichever Bear you choose.
findings.note: Addressed. The Bear prices the low end of the guide and argues 12x on that outcome plus stock-based compensation; finalRecommendation now places a miss below the Bear.

findings.quote: Card economics: if cashback keeps growing faster than interchange, card adoption reduces net revenue rather than adding to it.
findings.issue: The mechanism is wrong as stated. In Q2'26 cashback already grew faster than interchange in percentage terms ($3.0 million from $2.5 million against $5.9 million from $5.3 million). Even so, interchange rose by more dollars than cashback, so the card still added to net revenue. Faster percentage growth on a smaller base does not by itself turn the card's contribution negative. That needs cashback to rise by more dollars than interchange. As written, the risk describes today's condition and says it reduces net revenue, which the quarter's figures do not show.
findings.fix: State the risk as cashback rising by more than interchange in dollars, which would narrow and eventually reverse the card's net contribution. Keep the watch item on the gap between the two lines.
findings.note: Addressed. The risk now says interchange still rose by more dollars, and frames the risk as cashback rising by more dollars; the exec-summary risk matches.

findings.quote: The $1.90–$2.50 target range brackets the Base and stops at the low end of the Street's target range on the upside.
findings.issue: Only the upper end of the band is explained. Nothing says how $1.90 was set relative to the Base ($2.14) or the Bear ($1.58).
findings.fix: Add a clause giving the basis for the $1.90 low end, in words, relative to the scenarios.
findings.note: Addressed. The $1.80 low end is explained relative to the Base and the Bear (it is about 45% of the way down), and the $2.20 high end relative to the price.

findings.quote: the earnings release reports non-GAAP net income of $3.4 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $6.6 million; the difference from GAAP is stock-based compensation, which non-GAAP net income excludes by definition
findings.issue: Coming after both measures, 'the difference from GAAP is stock-based compensation' reads as covering Adjusted EBITDA too. The release defines Adjusted EBITDA as also excluding taxes, other income, net, and depreciation and amortization.
findings.fix: Limit the sentence to non-GAAP net income, for example: 'non-GAAP net income differs from the GAAP net loss by stock-based compensation, which was 7,211 in the quarter'.
findings.note: Addressed. Now limited to non-GAAP net income.

findings.quote: the MD&A cites higher amortization of capitalized software, partly offset by savings from using AI in place of human agents, and Visa volume incentives that reduce cost of revenue fell to $0.2 million from $0.8 million
findings.issue: The Visa clause is part of the 'MD&A cites' sentence, so it reads as one of the reasons the MD&A gives for the margin decline. The MD&A reports the incentive amounts but does not cite them as a cause of higher cost of revenue.
findings.fix: Move the Visa figures into their own sentence, stated as reported amounts: 'Separately, Visa volume incentives, which reduce cost of revenue, were $0.2 million against $0.8 million'.
findings.note: Addressed. The MD&A's causes are stated as written; the Visa amounts are in their own sentence.

findings.quote: driven by pre-IPO RSUs with approximately three years of vesting remaining
findings.issue: Drops the source's hedge. The release says the estimate is 'driven primarily by the pre-IPO grant of RSUs'.
findings.fix: Write 'driven primarily by pre-IPO RSUs'.
findings.note: Addressed. 'driven primarily' restored.

findings.quote: The counter-case is the Street
findings.issue: Tic. 'The counter-case' opens or frames a sentence in multiplesCommentary, balanceCommentary ('The counter-case to a comfortable balance sheet'), moatFactors[1] ('The counter-case is economic') and growth.points[1] ('The counter-case is consensus'). capitalAllocation adds 'The counter-point is'. incomeCommentary uses 'Our view:', which the desk lists as a tic to avoid.
findings.fix: Keep the counter-arguments but vary how they are introduced (for example 'Against that', or state the opposing figure directly). Replace 'Our view:' with a plain concluding sentence.
findings.note: Addressed. 'The counter-case' and 'Our view:' are gone; the counter-arguments are introduced in varied ways.

findings.quote: the MD&A says month-to-month arrangements can be terminated by either party without penalty, so the base offers limited lock-in
findings.issue: Half the source. The MD&A also describes annual arrangements based on a minimum number of monthly members, where early termination requires paying the remaining obligation plus fees. It does not give the mix. 'Limited lock-in' is drawn from the month-to-month half only.
findings.fix: Note that annual arrangements carry termination payments and that the excerpt does not give the mix, then reach the lock-in view on that basis.
findings.note: Addressed. Annual arrangements with early-termination payments are noted, and the undisclosed mix qualifies the lock-in view.

findings.quote: Consensus does not yet reflect it
findings.issue: Characterizes what analysts have modeled, which the surface does not show. Consensus gives only the revenue and EPS figures. It may already include New Expensify growth, netted against the Classic decline.
findings.fix: State what the figures show, for example: 'Consensus revenue does not show it yet:' followed by the FY26E and FY27E figures.
findings.note: Deferred to the next synthesis; editing the judgment after the final re-check would leave it unreviewed. Reviewer accepts the decline.

findings.quote: below the price by more than the SELL line allows
findings.issue: Repeated phrase. analystCommentary says the weighting 'lands below the current price by more than the SELL line allows', and finalRecommendation says the weighted value 'sits below the price by more than the SELL line allows'.
findings.fix: Keep the phrase in one place and word the other differently, or have analystCommentary point to the recommendation.
findings.note: Deferred to the next synthesis; editing the judgment after the final re-check would leave it unreviewed. Reviewer accepts the decline.
